title: Logic Lights circuit catalogue
description: Everything a circuit *declares* — what it is called, where it sits in the picker, and how the app should present it. What a circuit *does* is code, and lives in web/js/behaviour/<id>.js keyed by the same id. See docs/DATA.md for where that boundary falls and why.

groupOrder.description: Picker section order. A group is 'Technology · Subsection', or just 'Technology' for a section with no subsections. Groups named here but unused simply do not appear; groups used but not named here are appended at the end.

id.description: Stable identifier. Used in the URL hash, and the key that binds this entry to its behaviour module.

group.description: Which picker section this belongs in. Must appear in groupOrder, and must match the devices the circuit is actually built from — the test suite checks that a circuit in 'CMOS' really does use complementary pairs.

name.description: Display name, shown in the picker and the title bar.

title.description: A few words naming what this circuit demonstrates, shown beside the name in the status row — 'the 4004's real ADD datapath', 'an odd number of inversions never settles'. Not a sentence: it sits inline after an em dash, so it reads as a subtitle rather than prose. Keep it under about 60 characters; the status row is one line and truncates.

brief.description: One or two sentences opening the info panel: what the reader is looking at and why it is worth looking at. This is the only prose most readers will see, so it carries the idea, not the implementation. The line-by-line story goes in `walkthrough` and the construction details in `engineering`.

walkthrough.description: A line-by-line account of what the circuit does when it runs, shown as the info panel's first tab. Written for machines, whose ROM holds a program worth narrating step by step; circuits with no instruction stream omit it. Every value quoted here is checked against a real headless run by the test suite, so it cannot drift from the hardware the way a hand-maintained comment does.

intro.description: Optional sentence or two before the steps, framing what the program as a whole is doing.

at.description: ROM address this step executes, matching the trace's execAddr. Two consecutive steps share an address only when the instruction genuinely takes two instruction cycles, as FIN does.

op.description: The disassembled instruction, e.g. 'ADD r0'. Checked against the disassembler so it cannot disagree with the ROM's actual bytes.

state.description: The machine state after this step, as displayed keys — 'ACC': '14', 'CY': '1'. Asserted against a real run: every key must name a lamp bus the circuit has, and every value must match what the hardware settles to.

text.description: What is happening and why it matters. The reason this step is in the program rather than a restatement of the opcode.

outro.description: Optional closing note — what the program does on its next lap, or what to watch for a second time around.

desc.description: Engineering detail: how the thing is actually built, which trade-offs were taken, and which bugs the construction is shaped to avoid. Shown under the info panel's 'Engineering detail' tab, for the reader who wants the construction rather than the idea. The one-line summary lives in `title`, the introduction in `brief`.

hints.description: Caption per bus in the I/O table, keyed by bus name. Bus names come from switch and lamp labels via the trailing-digit rule (A0..A3 group into bus A), so a hint keyed to an individual switch will never appear — the tests check every key names a real bus.

table.description: A legend of selector codes, for circuits whose input is a code rather than a number. The live row highlights, so it doubles as an indicator of what the circuit is currently doing. The row-picking function lives in the behaviour module as `select`.

code.description: The literal code, e.g. '011'. Use an x for a don't-care bit ('11x') when several codes share a row.

note.description: Short gloss shown beside the name. Hidden in compact layouts, so nothing essential belongs here.

state.description: A grid of live internal values the circuit's own outputs do not expose — a register file's stored words, or every function an ALU computed. The reader function lives in the behaviour module as `read`, and must read the circuit's nets rather than recomputing: a display doing its own arithmetic would agree with a broken circuit.

columns.description: Grid columns. Pick so the rows divide evenly — 4 for sixteen registers, 3 for six ALU functions.

key.description: Legend under the grid, explaining any highlighting. Hidden in compact layouts.
